searchText: Oh btw in case anyone missed it: https://ethresear.ch/t/what-would-break-if-we-lose-address-collision-resistance/11356 I think this does solidify my impression that this 14 byte hash middle ground is a bad idea though Does anyone have any experience with blockchains that assign account numbers sequentially? Particularly, how do they deal with sending money to users that do not have accounts yet Oh btw totally random but I think onion websites are one example of a place where you have a hash that's long enough for brute force resistance but not collision resistance https://bitcoin.stackexchange.com/questions/30494/how-is-a-nxt-account-address-generated-why-do-we-need-to-send-out-a-transaction Oh I see This does open a path for a different kind of backwards compatibility layer, basically have a way to create addresses that *are* sequentially assigned, with an on-chain mapping pre-committing to the initcode hash of those addresses
